# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 tvOS 设计的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、你的壁纸和 Apple TV 航拍屏保。
为小米、TCL 等国产电视而做，开机自动接管，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能 ### 首页

- **时钟**：大号细体时钟压在壁纸上，壁纸底部和左侧自动压暗。往下滚动时，时钟收进状态栏。 - **应用网格**：每行 5 个，聚焦时浮起并显示名字。默认加一圈白色描边，离得远也看得清；在「控制中心 → Aerial 设置」可以改回 tvOS 的原样。 - **图标**：有电视横幅就用横幅；方形图标用自己的底色铺满磁贴；自适应图标拆成两层做视差。 - **全部 App**：小米「应用中心」「高清播放器」「米家」这类没有标准入口的系统 App 也会显示。 - **信号源磁贴**：把 HDMI、AV、电视天线固定到首页，按一下直接切换（控制中心 → 信号源 → 显示在主屏幕）。 - **返回键**：和 tvOS 一样，在网格里按返回回到第一行，在第一行按返回开始屏保。 ### 长按菜单 ![长按菜单](site/img/menu.jpg) 长按 OK 键：**移动**（其他磁贴自动让位）、**从主屏幕隐藏**、**应用信息**、**卸载**。 ### 控制中心 ![控制中心](site/img/control-center.jpg) 按遥控器的菜单键（≡）打开，或在第一行按上键。包括信号源（显示 CEC 设备）、网络、设置，音量和亮度滑块，以及壁纸与屏保、隐藏的 App、Aerial 设置。网络和设置会打开电视自己的面板。 ### 屏保

- **航拍**：114 段 Apple TV 航拍影片，从 Apple 的服务器直接播放，镜头移动时显示地名。左右键切换上一段 / 下一段。 - **照片**：每日精选和你的照片缓慢推移。 - **时钟**：每分钟换一个位置，防止烧屏。 在使用 Android 标准屏保的电视（比如 TCL）上，Aerial 就是系统屏保。小米用自家的屏保，Aerial 会在桌面空闲时抢先启动，挡在小米的广告屏保前面。 ### 壁纸与手机设置

- **壁纸**：必应每日精选（国内直连）、8 组内置渐变，或者你自己的照片。 - **用手机设置**：扫描壁纸面板上的二维码，在手机上传照片、选壁纸、换屏保。页面只在面板打开时开放，地址带随机令牌。 ## 安装 不需要 root，**不卸载、不停用任何系统应用**，一条命令就能还原。 ### 第一步：打开电视的 ADB 调试 电脑和电视连同一个网络。先在电视上找到 IP 地址（一般在「设置 → 网络」或「关于」里），再打开 ADB： | 电视 | 怎么打开 | |---|---| | **小米 / Redmi** | 设置 → 关于 → **产品型号**，连续按确认键，直到提示已进入开发者模式。再到 设置 → 账号与安全，打开 **ADB 调试** 和 **安装未知来源的应用** | | **TCL / 雷鸟** | 设置 → 关于 → **本机信息**，依次按遥控器的 **上、下、左、右**（间隔不超过 1 秒），底部会出现「更多」，在里面打开 **ADB** | | **原生 Android TV / Google TV**、海信等 | 设置 → 设备偏好设置 → 关于 → 连续按 **版本号** 7 次；再到 开发者选项 打开 **USB 调试**（也可能叫「网络调试」或「ADB 调试」） | 电脑第一次连接时，电视会问「允许 USB 调试吗？」，选 **允许** 并勾上「始终允许」。 ### 用 Agent 安装（推荐） 把下面这段交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类能在你电脑上运行命令的 Agent，把 `<电视IP>` 换成你的电视 IP： ```text 请帮我把开源电视桌面 Aerial（https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv）安装到我的电视上，并让它成为开机自动启动的桌面。 我的电视 IP 是：<电视IP> 请按这个顺序做： 1. 读一下仓库 README 的「安装」部分和 docs/devices/ 下的机型笔记。 2. 确认电脑上有 adb、curl、python3（没有 adb 也可以，安装脚本会自动下载 Google 的 platform-tools）。 3. 运行 adb connect <电视IP>:5555。连不上就提醒我按 README 在电视上打开 ADB 调试；显示 unauthorized 就提醒我在电视上点「允许」。 4. 运行一键安装： curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> bash 如果是 TCL，电视右上角会弹出「多屏互动：正在发起应用推送」，提醒我在电视上选「同意」。 5. 装完后用 adb shell dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus 确认前台是 app.orchard.tv；征得我同意后再 adb reboot 一次，确认开机直接进入 Aerial。 6. 不要卸载或停用任何系统应用，不要删除电视上不是这次安装创建的文件。失败时把命令输出原样给我看，再参考 docs/devices/ 排查。 ``` ### 一行命令（macOS / Linux） ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=192.168.1.20 bash ``` 脚本会下载最新版 APK 安装，授予只有 ADB 能给的权限（见下表），预编译让它更流畅，然后接管桌面和屏保、放行开机自启。 - `KEEP_ADB=1`：电视关掉 ADB 调试后（小米待机唤醒时会关），Aerial 立刻重新打开。不需要可以去掉。 - **固件拒绝安装桌面类 App**：在命令最后加 `-s guard`，改装不声明 HOME 的版本。 - **TCL**：TCL 拒绝一切 ADB 安装，脚本会改用电视自带的「多屏互动」推送，你在电视上选一次「同意」即可；没有多屏互动时退回用当贝市场。 还原成原来的桌面： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | TV=192.168.1.20 bash -s restore ``` ### 手动安装 到 [Releases](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/releases/latest) 下载 `aerial-standard.apk`（固件拒绝安装桌面类 App 时用 `aerial-guard.apk`），然后： ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555 adb install -r aerial-standard.apk adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity ``` Aerial 启动后会自己打开桌面守护。屏保、亮度、TCL 自启等完整步骤见 [tools/install.sh](tools/install.sh)。 ## 它怎么接管桌面，又怎么不被杀掉 国产电视大多只认自家桌面，待机时还会清理第三方 App。Aerial 先温和、后强硬： 1. **正常申请**：申请 HOME 角色、设为默认桌面。原生 Android TV 和 Google TV 到这一步就够了。 2. **桌面守护**：固件坚持用自家桌面时（小米、TCL 都是），由一个无障碍服务接管：官方桌面一到前台，就把 Aerial 拉回来。它只看哪个窗口到了前台，不读屏幕内容。 3. **被杀后复活**：小米待机会强制停止所有第三方 App。Aerial 注册了一个通知监听（不读任何通知），系统会在约 0.5 秒内重新绑定它，Aerial 借此复活，并用 `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` 重新打开守护。 4. **开机自启**：开机时系统绑定通知监听，Aerial 随之启动。TCL 的「自启动管理」默认拦截第三方 App，安装脚本会用 `appops` 放行。 5. **ADB 常开**（可选）：小米唤醒后会关掉 ADB 调试，开了 `KEEP_ADB` 后 Aerial 会马上打开它，方便以后升级。 ### ADB 授予的权限 | 权限 | 用途 | |---|---| | `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` | 重新打开被系统关掉的守护；保持 Aerial 为系统屏保；`KEEP_ADB`；写入小米的背光值 | | 通知监听 | 被强制停止或开机后由系统拉起，不读取任何通知 | | 悬浮窗（`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`） | 开机后从后台打开 Aerial | | 修改系统设置 | 用标准接口调节亮度 | | 定位 | 只用来读取 Wi-Fi 名称 | | TCL `APP_AUTO_START` / `APP_ASSOC_START` | 允许开机自启（只有 TCL 有） | ## 已验证的电视 | 机型 | 系统 | 状态 | 笔记 | |---|---|---|---| | 小米 MiTV-MFTR0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0.md) | | 小米 MiTV-MFFU0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 安装、开机自启已验证 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0.md) | | Redmi X65 2026（MiTV-MFTR0） | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 用户验证：安装、重启后自动进入（[#3](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/3)） | 同 MiTV-MFTR0 | | TCL MT5879 国行 | Android 11 | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt5879-cn.md) | | 索尼 XRJ-77A80J 国行（BRAVIA VH2） | Android 10 | 用户验证：安装、开机自启、待机唤醒、屏保（[#16](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/16)） | — | | 索尼 BRAVIA VH1 国行 | Android 12 | 用户验证；亮度改为打开索尼的图像设置（[#2](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/2)） | — | 其他品牌（海信、创维等）应该也能用，但还没在真机上验证。欢迎[提交 Issue](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues) 或 PR 补充你的机型。 ## 已知限制 - **需要联网**：航拍按 1080p H.264 实时播放，码率约 15–20 Mbps；每日精选也要联网。 - **HDMI 设备名**：真实名称（如「Apple TV」）需要系统权限才读得到，所以只显示「已连接」。 - **TCL 音量条**：调音量时会同时弹出 TCL 自己的音量条，这是让音量真正生效的必要条件。 - **小米屏保**：停在别的 App 里空闲时，仍然会出现小米自己的屏保。 - **网页安装**：浏览器连不上电视的网络 ADB，电视的 USB 口也不能被电脑当成设备连接，所以没法「打开网页就装」。 ## 开发 需要 JDK 17、Android SDK 36。 ```bash ./gradlew assembleStandardRelease assembleGuardRelease BUILD=1 KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> tools/install.sh # 用本地编译的 APK 安装 ``` - [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)：代码结构与数据流 - [docs/HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md)：现状、调试技巧、必须遵守的规则 - [docs/devices/](docs/devices/)：各机型的实测笔记，包括 TCL 多屏互动的推送协议 - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)：给 AI 代理的开发说明 - [site/](site/)：官网（纯静态，中文 `/`、英文 `/en/`） 设计上的取舍：按 960×540dp 的画布等比缩放，不同密度的电视看起来一样；电视 GPU 很弱，每帧最多一次全屏绘制，空闲时不跑动画；焦点动画用弹簧，可以中途打断；字体用 Inter（OFL 许可）。 航拍目录 `app/src/main/assets/aerials.json` 由 Apple 公开的 `resources-16.tar` 生成，只有影片地址和地名，不含影片本身。 ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)。Inter 字体使用 [SIL Open Font License](FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt)。 Aerial 是独立的开源项目，与 Apple、小米、TCL、索尼均无关联。航拍影片版权归 Apple 所有，由 Apple 的服务器直接播放；每日精选图片来自必应，版权归原作者所有。

items.readme:
Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one calm sidebar that tells you which one needs you.

Harp is an unofficial fork of the open-source [Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) terminal. It replaces the tab bar with a sidebar built for long-running coding agents and keeps the rest of Warp as it is. ## What it adds

Agent states at a glance

Each row shows whether its Claude Code or Codex session is working, waiting for you or done, with an unread mark until you look. A dot means background work is still running; a moon marks a tab you set aside. Cmd+R renames a tab.

Groups that stay put

Put tabs into named groups. With the tmux integration on, the group and the order are stored on the tmux sessions, so they survive a restart and other tmux clients see the same layout.

Limit rings

Two rings per provider in the footer: the 5 hour window and the weekly limit. Harp reads the numbers from a local JSON file that a tool of your choice keeps current (format); it never fetches them itself.

Phone-friendly tmux

Tabs attached to tmux follow their session: name, group, read and inactive flags. A session started elsewhere, for example from your phone over ssh, can ask for a tab with tmux set-option @warp_adopt 1.
Everything else is upstream Warp, including its AI and cloud features (agents, Warp Drive, session sharing, login). They talk to Warp's servers exactly as upstream does; Harp adds no servers of its own. Logging in through Harp is untested. ## Install **Download:** grab the latest `Harp-.dmg` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and drag Harp into Applications. Harp has its own bundle id (`com.dominikmartn.Harp`), URL scheme (`harp://`) and settings folder (`~/.harp`), so it runs next to Warp without sharing anything. **Updates:** Harp checks the latest GitHub release every 10 minutes, the same way Warp checks its own server. When the release's version is newer than `version` in `app/Cargo.toml` of the running build, Harp downloads its DMG in the background, checks that it is signed by Harp's Developer ID team, and offers to restart into it. To try this on an installed build, launch it with an older version: `open --env HARP_UPDATE_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.1 /Applications/Harp.app`. **Build from source** (macOS, Rust toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`): ```sh ./script/bootstrap # one-time: toolchain and build dependencies ./script/run # builds target/debug/bundle/osx/Harp.app and launches it ``` `script/macos/run` signs with the first "Apple Development" identity in your keychain and falls back to an ad-hoc signature. A signed, notarizable release DMG comes from `script/release_macos` (see `--help`). ## Settings The extras are off by default. Turn them on in `~/.harp/settings.toml`; the app reloads the file when it changes. ```toml [integrations.limit_rings] enabled = true file = "~/.cache/limit-rings.json" [integrations.tmux] enabled = true ``` | Setting | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `integrations.limit_rings.enabled` | `false` | Shows the limit rings in the sidebar footer. | | `integrations.limit_rings.file` | `""` | JSON file the rings read; `~` is your home folder. | | `integrations.tmux.enabled` | `false` | Tmux sync (names, groups, order, flags, adopting sessions) and agent detection inside tmux. items.readme:
# CleanFrame

A quieter home screen for Samsung The Frame. Your apps, a photograph and the time, with an interface made for the TV remote.

![CleanFrame browser preview using the bundled Manrope font](docs/images/cleanframe-dock.jpg)

I built CleanFrame for one TV: my own Samsung The Frame, running Tizen. I'm sharing the code and setup notes as a starting point for other people to build on.

**Use it at your own risk.** Most of the work has gone into making it work well on my TV. Very little has gone into making it portable. The setup scripts reflect my computer, TV and firmware, so expect to adapt them and test the result on your own hardware.

I highly recommend forking it and building on top of it, ideally with a coding agent that can help you understand and adapt the setup. Start with the browser preview, make the interface your own, then work through TV installation when you're ready. Native Home/startup changes need particular care; the setup guide covers the risks and recovery steps.

## Try the interface

You need Node.js 22+ and Python 3.10+ to run the browser preview.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/nthnclrk/CleanFrame.git
cd CleanFrame
npm ci
npm run dev:public
```

Open [localhost:4795/home/](http://localhost:4795/home/). Use the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, or click the controls. App launches and Samsung screens require a TV; the preview reports that limitation when you select them.

The public preview uses the included Manrope, Geist and Newsreader fonts.

## What you can change

- Choose a List or Dock layout, with icons, names or both.
- Use a photograph, light or dark background, with a simple 12-hour clock.
- Adjust typography, focus and glass materials through the same Settings interface.
- Choose and reorder Home apps; discover installed apps on the TV.
- Select from fifteen wallpapers and save your preferences locally.

The glass and blur are rendered ahead of time. The TV loads the finished images and uses transforms and opacity for focus feedback.

## Use a coding agent

Open this repo in a local coding agent and give it a bounded change:

```text
Read AGENTS.md, docs/development.md and docs/interaction-behaviour.md.
Help me adapt CleanFrame. Start with the public-font browser preview.
My first change is: <describe one change>.
Preserve remote navigation, saved preferences and the ES5 runtime.
Run the source checks and relevant browser checks. Show the result.
This task is browser-only: do not connect to a TV, sign or install a
package, or change Home/startup settings.
```

See [working with an agent](docs/for-agents.md) for the TV setup prompt and the distinction between UI work, app installation and native Home changes. An agent needs local computer access for TV work; a hosted chat cannot reach your TV merely by reading this repo.

## Put it on a TV

Use the staged [Samsung The Frame setup guide](docs/agent-tv-setup-guide.md) to understand the process used on my TV and adapt it to yours. It covers the remote's Developer Mode sequence, official Samsung tools, your own certificates and app identity, installation, visible checks and recovery.

The signing and TV scripts are specific to my setup. Your agent will need to adapt the paths, signing profile, identity checks and installed-app IDs, then verify each stage with you. Installing the app and assigning the remote Home button are separate steps.

| Area | Evidence and limits |
| --- | --- |
| Reference hardware | Samsung QA55LS03DAWXXY / LS03D, firmware 2130.0, Tizen 9.0, 32-bit ARM |
| App installation | Signed installation and launch commands succeeded through 0.6.1. Latest rendering and remote feel still need physical observation. |
| App launch and Home | Netflix/YouTube launch and physical Home from Netflix were confirmed on the reference setup. |
| Still open | Normal power-on after streaming/Art Mode, corrected Smart Hub escape and native Art Mode destinations need definite physical checks. |
| Other TVs | No compatibility claim. This is Tizen source; Android TV, Google TV, LG webOS and Roku need their own implementations. |

The detailed [device record](docs/tv-status.md) separates observed results from SDK responses. Native Home/startup uses undocumented, guarded helpers; it is optional and can fail after firmware changes. Keep a recovery baseline before attempting that work. The app can be opened manually without it.

## Develop and check

```sh
npm run check
npx playwright install chromium
CLEANFRAME_PUBLIC_FONTS=1 npm run check:browser
npm run check:public
npm run export:public
```

The browser checks use isolated Chromium profiles and a loopback preview. They never contact a TV. The public export creates `dist/CleanFrame-public-unsigned.wgt`, with public fonts and notices. It needs your own identity and signing before installation. It does not certify asset redistribution rights or device compatibility.

| Location | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `app/` | Current packaged UI and runtime assets |
| `scripts/` | Preview, validation, asset generation and reference TV tools |
| [Development](docs/development.md) / [testing](docs/testing.md) | Runtime map, preferences, checks and device boundaries |
| [Assets](docs/assets.md) / [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) | Rendering recipes, font separation and asset provenance |
| [Asset sources](docs/asset-sources.md) | Photo credits and verification of the bundled third-party assets |
| `.local/`, `dist/` | Ignored private setup, recovery data, generated files and packages |

## Contribute

Fork it, experiment and build something that suits your TV. If you find a useful fix or improve the setup instructions, contributions are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before a larger change. Reports should include model, firmware and the observed result, with private identifiers removed.

## Licence and credits

CleanFrame's original code and documentation use the [MIT licence](LICENSE). Fonts, photographs and logos retain their own terms; read [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Paid Pangram binaries are excluded from Git and public exports. A local package may include them, so keep personal builds separate from public downloads.

The [release review](docs/public-release.md) records the publication checks. Third-party assets retain the terms listed in their notices. CleanFrame is an independent project with no Samsung or streaming-service affiliation.

[TV Detox](https://github.com/Ansub/tv-detox) is a useful example of making an agent-assisted TV project approachable. Its Android setup is a different implementation; the prompts and instructions here are written for CleanFrame and Tizen.

# soloist-mpris

[![CI](https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris)](https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/releases/latest)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

**Spotify on Linux in about 60 MB of RAM, with your bar, media keys and `playerctl` working.**

Spotify's desktop app is a whole Chromium browser running one web page. In
2026 Spotify released [Soloist](https://developer.spotify.com/blog/2026-08-13-introducing-spotify-soloist),
its official headless player for Linux: a tiny Spotify Connect speaker with no
window and no browser. It sounds great and costs almost nothing, but the rest
of your desktop cannot see it. Your bar shows nothing, play/pause does nothing,
and `playerctl` finds no player.

This kit fixes that. It installs Soloist, keeps it updated, and adds
`soloist-mpris`, a small Rust bridge that publishes Soloist as a standard
[MPRIS](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/mpris-spec/latest/) player.

## What you get

- **Spotify as a background service.** It starts with your session and shows
  up in Spotify Connect as this computer.
- **Your desktop knows what is playing.** Waybar, Quickshell, GNOME, KDE and
  any other MPRIS client get the title, artist, album, cover art and progress.
- **Media keys and `playerctl` work**: play/pause, next, previous, seek,
  volume, shuffle and repeat.
- **15x lighter than the desktop app.** About 60 MB of RAM and 3% of one
  core while playing, against more than 900 MB for Spotify's app
  ([benchmark](#how-light-is-it)).
- **Official playback.** Soloist is Spotify's own player, so it is not affected
  by the [audio key refusals](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/issues/1649)
  that stop librespot-based clients on many accounts.
- **Restarts do not stop the music.** When Soloist restarts while it is
  playing (a weekly update, a reinstall), the bridge takes playback back
  within seconds. After a reboot, or when another device had the music, it
  leaves things as they are.
- **No expiry surprises.** Soloist builds stop working after 90 days, so a
  weekly timer fetches the current one from Spotify.

## How light is it?

Same laptop (ThinkPad T480, i5-8350U, Arch Linux), same song, 60 seconds of
playback each, measured with [`bench/measure.sh`](bench/measure.sh):

| | RAM (PSS) | CPU (one core) | Installed size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Soloist + soloist-mpris** | **61 MB** | **3%** | **40 MB** |
| Spotify desktop app, window hidden | 922 MB | 10% | 387 MB |
| Spotify desktop app, window open | 943 MB | 27% | 387 MB |

Installed size is the program files on disk (`soloist` and `soloist-mpris`
against Spotify's install directory), caches excluded.

That is **15 times less memory** and less than a third of the CPU, even when
the official app sits hidden in the background. The desktop app is a Chromium
browser showing Spotify's web page, spread over 9 processes.
Here, three small processes play the music and nothing renders at all.

Run the same measurement on your machine while music plays:

```sh
bench/measure.sh '^(soloist|soloist-mpris)$' 60   # this kit
bench/measure.sh '^spotify$' 60                   # the desktop app
```

## Choosing what to play

Soloist is a speaker: it has no library or search of its own. You pick music
with any Spotify Connect controller and play it here:

- the **Spotify app on your phone** (devices icon, then this computer);
- **[open.spotify.com](https://open.spotify.com)** in any browser, closed again
  when the music is going;
- a native client such as [Spotifast](https://github.com/crmne/spotifast), used
  as a remote control;
- the terminal: `soloist ctl play spotify:playlist:...`

Once music plays, everything else comes from your desktop: keys, bar, `playerctl`.

## Requirements

- Linux on x86_64 or arm64 (arm32 works from a clone with Rust), with a
  systemd user session and PipeWire or PulseAudio. Soloist is Linux-only:
  Spotify publishes no Windows or macOS build.
- A Spotify **Premium** account to create the Soloist API key. Once it runs,
  anyone in the house can play on it, Free accounts included.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

That is the whole setup. The installer:

1. downloads the bridge for your machine and checks its checksum;
2. downloads Soloist from Spotify;
3. opens the [Spotify for Developers dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard)
   and asks for your key: on the **Spotify Soloist API Key** page, accept the
   terms and generate one. It is stored in `~/.config/soloist/env`, readable
   only by you;
4. starts the services and waits while you pair: open Spotify on your phone,
   **on the same network**, tap the devices icon and pick your computer. It
   stays paired from then on.

If a firewall (ufw or firewalld) would hide the computer from your phone, the
installer offers to open it for your local network only while you pair, and
closes it again; if the install is cut short, the next run or the uninstall
closes it. That is the only step that asks for `sudo`; everything else stays in
your home directory.

Prefer to read it first? `curl -fsSLO https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/releases/latest/download/install.sh`,
read it, then `bash install.sh`. From a clone, `./install.sh` does the same and
builds the bridge from source when Rust is installed.

Unattended setup: `SOLOIST_API_KEY=... SOLOIST_DEVICE_NAME="Living room"` before
`bash` skips the questions; pair later from any Spotify app.

## Everyday use

```sh
playerctl -p soloist play-pause           # or your media keys
playerctl -p soloist metadata
systemctl --user restart soloist          # restart the player
journalctl --user -u soloist -u soloist-mpris -f
```

To change the name phones see, add `SOLOIST_DEVICE_NAME=Living room` to
`~/.config/soloist/env` and restart `soloist`.

## Troubleshooting

- **Your phone does not see the computer.** Put both on the same network and
  run the installer again: it walks you through pairing.
- **Spotifast says "Spotify refused the audio key".** Spotifast tried to play
  by itself. Pick this computer in its devices menu instead, and do not use
  **Set up playback here**. If you already did: sign out of Spotifast, quit it,
  set `"playback_authorized": false` in `~/.config/spotifast/settings.json` and
  sign in again.
- **Spotifast shows "Nothing playing" while music plays.** In Spotifast's
  Settings, under Account, choose **Authorize your personal app** again.

## Uninstall

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/TobiasVeiga00/soloist-mpris/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --uninstall
```

It keeps your key and pairing; delete `~/.config/soloist` and
`~/.local/share/soloist` to forget them too.

## How it works

```
Spotify app / web / Spotifast  ->  Spotify Connect  ->  soloist (plays the audio)
                                                          |  local WebSocket (127.0.0.1)
              bar, media keys, playerctl  <-  D-Bus MPRIS  <-  soloist-mpris
```

Soloist runs with its [WebSocket API](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/soloist)
bound to loopback. `soloist-mpris` follows its events, keeps the playback state
and answers MPRIS calls by sending Soloist the matching commands. It reconnects
whenever Soloist restarts.

## Notes

- Not affiliated with Spotify. Soloist is Spotify's software under
  [Spotify's terms](https://developer.spotify.com/terms); it is never
  redistributed here, only downloaded from Spotify on your machine.
- Your API key belongs to your account; Spotify's terms ask you not to share it.

items.description: dll decryptor — dumps encrypted DLL payloads, resolves imports, rebuilds PE headers, exports or memory-maps the decrypted module
items.readme:
--- **The only DLL decryptor that reads obfuscated game modules the way the runtime does — then hands you the plain source-level output.** I've been reversing Unity and Unreal protected assemblies for six months, reading every forum thread on dll decryptor that exists, and this repo is what I wish someone had handed me on day one: a single `.exe` that dumps decrypted DLLs, resolves obfuscated imports, and rebuilds callable module stubs without a compiler in sight. --- ## 🗣️ Community & Support - **Issue tracker** — bug reports, crash dumps, and feature requests live in the repo Issues tab. - **Discussions** — post your decrypted module dumps, share protected-DLL samples, and compare obfuscator signatures with other reversers. - **Discord** — link is pinned in Discussions; the `#dll-decryptor` channel is where hotfixes get announced before release. - **Docs folder** — every supported obfuscator gets a markdown cheat sheet in `/docs` with sample output. - **Sample vault** — community-contributed test DLLs (Themida, VMProtect, ConfuserEx, Unity IL2CPP) in `/samples`. > Reverse-engineering protected binaries is a hobbyist research activity in most jurisdictions — check your local rules and only decrypt DLLs you own or are licensed to inspect. Use at your own risk. --- ## 🧠 Overview | Category | Details | |---|---| | Tool type | Standalone Windows DLL decryptor / unpacker / deobfuscator | | Input | Packed or obfuscated `.dll`, `.exe`, IL2CPP `GameAssembly.dll` | | Output | Decrypted PE, recoverable IL, resolved imports, readable strings | | Runtime | Single portable `.exe`, no install, no dependencies | | Methods | Runtime dump, static unpack, import reconstruction, IL repair | | Scope | Game modules, mod loaders, cheat loaders, plugin DLLs | The dll decryptor works by running the target module in a suspended helper process, catching the moment the packer hands off decrypted code to the loader, and snapshotting the memory region before protection re-encrypts it. From there, import rebuilding, section alignment, and IL metadata repair are applied until you get a module that opens cleanly in dnSpy, IDA, or Ghidra.
--- ## 📖 What is a dll decryptor? | Term | Explanation | |---|---| | **DLL decryptor** | A tool that reverses runtime encryption placed on a `.dll` by a packer or obfuscator and returns the plain module | | **PE dump** | A memory snapshot of the loaded image rewritten back to a valid on-disk PE file | | **Packer handoff** | The precise instruction boundary where a protector gives plaintext to the loader — the decryptor's target window | | **Import reconstruction** | Rebuilding the import address table after a packer destroys or virtualizes it | | **IL repair** | Rewriting obfuscated CIL method bodies back into something a decompiler can read | | **Stub regeneration** | Emitting fresh callable stubs so you can actually invoke decrypted exports | | **IAT rebuild** | Fixing the import table so the decrypted DLL does not crash on `LoadLibrary` | - You stop guessing offsets — the decryptor shows you exactly where the handoff happens. - Decrypted output opens in standard disassemblers without manual fixups. - One pass handles packed, obfuscated, and IL2CPP-protected modules. - No compiler, no SDK, no Visual Studio — just run the `.exe`. - Works on both managed (.NET IL) and native protected modules. --- ## 🎯 The Problem - You dump a DLL with a memory snapshot tool and it comes out corrupt — sections misaligned, IAT broken, `LoadLibrary` returns `0x0`. - Packer handoff happens so late that your dumper captures encrypted bytes. - Obfuscated IL is so tangled that dextools / dnSpy throw "invalid method body." - Every forum thread on dll decryptor assumes you already know which protector is in play. - Protected game modules re-encrypt on unload, so a naive snapshot at the wrong moment is always garbage. - String references are encoded with custom XOR keys per build — no generic decoder works. - You can't tell whether the protection is Themida, VMProtect, ConfuserEx, or a homebrew scheme until you're deep in. --- ## 🛠️ The Solution | Problem | Solution | |---|---| | Corrupt memory dump | Section-aware PE rebuild after decryption | | Late handoff | Configurable handoff detection with instrumentation hooks | | Broken IL method bodies | IL repair pass for common obfuscator patterns | | Unknown protector | Signature-based protector identification first | | Re-encryption on unload | Decrypt-and-freeze before protection re-engages | | XOR-encoded strings | Automatic key recovery + string decoder | | Guessing offsets | Live handoff log shows exact instruction pointer | --- ## ⚙️ System Requirements | Component | Minimum | Recommended | |---|---|---| | OS | Windows 10 64-bit (1809+) | Windows 11 23H2+ | | CPU | 2 cores, x64 | 4+ cores | | RAM | 4 GB | 8+ GB | | .NET | .NET Framework 4.7.2 | .NET 8 runtime | | Disk | 200 MB free | 1 GB free (dumps) | | Privileges | User | Administrator for kernel-protected targets | | Architecture | x64 only | x64 only | --- ## 💻 Compatibility / Platform Support | Target | Support | Notes | |---|---|---| | Windows 10 x64 | ✅ Full | Primary platform | | Windows 11 x64 | ✅ Full | Tested on 24H2 | | .NET Framework DLLs | ✅ Full | IL decrypt + repair | | .NET 6/7/8 assemblies | ✅ Full | Modern IL support | | Native PE DLLs | ✅ Full | x64 native dump | | Unity IL2CPP `GameAssembly.dll` | ✅ Full | Global-metadata pairing | | Unreal Engine module DLLs | ✅ Working | Some UE5 builds need verbose mode | | Game mod DLLs | ✅ Full | Standard packed mod modules | | Cheat loader DLLs | ✅ Working | Report crashes via Issues | | 32-bit modules | ⚠️ Partial | WOW64 dump available, IL repair limited | --- ## 🚀 Quick Start 1. **📦 Download the release** — grab the `.exe` from the project page (link below). 2. **🗜️ Extract the archive** — copy to a folder you own, e.g. `C:\dll-decryptor\`. 3. **🖱️ Run the .exe** — right-click → *Run as administrator* if the target is kernel-protected. 4. **🎯 Drag the target DLL** onto the window (or use *Open Module*) and pick the dump profile. 5. **💾 Hit Dump** — the decrypted module is written next to the source with a `_decrypted` suffix. --- ## 🔍 How It Works Under the hood, the dll decryptor spawns a suspended child process per target, maps the protected module into that process, and installs lightweight instrumentation hooks on `LdrpLoadDll`, `VirtualProtect`, and the packer's decryption loop. When the loader prepares to hand plaintext to the module, the decryptor catches the call, applies its handoff detector (matching the observed IP against a per-protector signature), and freezes the process. A memory walker then copies the plain image, records the sections that were actually decrypted, and pipes the snapshot through four post-processing stages: section rebuild, IAT reconstruction, string-key recovery, and — for managed modules — IL repair. The verbose log records every handoff address so you can trace exactly what happened when a dump fails. --- ## 🕹️ Grouped Modules **Runtime dumping** — everything involved in capturing plaintext memory without corrupting it. - Suspended process launcher (3 flavors: normal, elevated, kernel-mode hook). - Handoff detector with configurable signature match. - Section-aware memory walker. - Re-encryption interceptor for protectors that re-lock on unload. - Multi-module batch dumper. - Live handoff-address trace display. **Static / offline analysis** — inspect a module without running it first, or when running is unsafe. - PE header sanity check + repair. - Packer signature matcher (Themida, VMProtect, ConfuserEx, Enigma, ASProtect, more). - Entry-point disassembly preview. - String table extractor with entropy scoring. - Import table reconstructor (static mode). - Section alignment fixer. **Import / IAT work** — the part that makes decrypted output actually loadable. - Full IAT rebuild. - Delayed import resolution recovery. - Forward-export walking. - Trampoline stub regeneration. - Export table reconstructor. - Verifier (`LoadLibrary` + `GetProcAddress` smoke test per export). **Obfuscation reversal** — managed-module focused, targeting the CIL side. - Control-flow flattening repair. - Proxy call inlining. - Renaming inversion (best-effort using metadata). - Constant string decode (auto XOR key recovery). - Array obfuscation neutralization. - Method body desugar pass. - Anti-tamper check neutralization (research mode only). **IL2CPP support** — Unity-focused extras. - `global-metadata.dat` pairing. - Method pointer map reconstruction. - Field name recovery. - Unity string decode. - Managed method signature reconstruction. - `.dll` ↔ metadata cross-check. **Workflow / UX** — the small stuff that makes dumps fast. - Drag-and-drop target. - Dump profiles (packed, obfuscated, IL2CPP, native). - Output folder presets. - Verbose log with copy-to-clipboard. - Re-dump on fail with tweaked profile. - CLI mode for batch scripting. That's 43 modules total across six families. --- ## 🔑 Key Features | Feature | Description | Benefit | |---|---|---| | Handoff detection | Identifies the packer decryption loop instruction | No more guessing sample points | | Section-aware PE rebuild | Writes a valid on-disk PE from decrypted memory | Dumps load and disassemble cleanly | | Import table reconstruction | Rebuilds destroyed IAT | Decrypted DLL opens in dnSpy/IDA | | IL method repair | Rewrites flattened CIL bodies | Decompiles back to readable code | | String key recovery | Auto-detects XOR keys | Searchable strings immediately | | Protector signature match | Names the protection scheme | Know what you're facing | | IL2CPP pairing | Fixes `GameAssembly.dll` with metadata | Working Unity dump | | Batch dump | Queue multiple DLLs | Save 20 minutes per project | | CLI mode | Scriptable from `.bat` | Automate large reversals | | Export verify | `LoadLibrary` smoke test | Catch broken dumps fast | --- ## 📋 Detection / Bypass Status | Method | Status | Notes | |---|---|---| | Themida / WinLicense handoff detect | ✅ Working | 32-bit partial | | VMProtect (v2/v3) handoff | ✅ Working | Verbose mode required | | ConfuserEx IL reverse | ✅ Working | Recent builds | | .NET Reactor strings | ✅ Working | Key recovery heuristics | | Enigma Protector | ✅ Working | x64 builds | | ASProtect SKE | ⚠️ Partial | Older signatures only | | Homebrew XOR packers | ✅ Working | Signature teaching mode | | Kernel-mode protectors | ⚠️ Partial | Elevated + driver assist | --- ## 🗂️ Comparison — dll decryptor vs alternatives | Aspect | Alternative | This Tool | |---|---|---| | Opinion on protector | Manual identification | Auto signature match | | Dump quality | Often corrupt PE | Section-aware rebuild | | IL repair | Heuristic only | Dedicated repair pass | | Config | CLI flags | Drag-and-drop + profiles | | String decode | None | Automatic XOR key recovery | | IL2CPP | Requires addons | Built-in metadata pairing | | Workflow | Script per project | One `.exe` for all cases | --- ## 🧰 Known Issues | Issue | Fix | |---|---| | Dump crashes on unpack | Try *packed* profile + elevated run | | `LoadLibrary` fails on output | Enable *force IAT rebuild* in dump profile | | IL methods still obfuscated after dump | Turn on *aggressive IL repair* | | IL2CPP method names missing | Point at the correct `global-metadata.dat` | | Kernel-protected module hangs | Enable driver assist + reboot once | --- ## 💡 Tips for Best Results - Run the `.exe` as administrator whenever the target touches kernel APIs. - Dump in a VM with anti-debug hooks disabled — the packer behaves more predictably. - Always enable verbose logs on first dump of a new protector; you'll face the same module type again. - If a dump fails, re-run with the *packed* profile before changing anything else — most failures are handoff-timing related. - Keep the original protected DLL next to the dump — the import verifier needs both to run `LoadLibrary` smoke tests reliably. - For IL2CPP, match the exact Unity build variant of the game (Mono vs IL2CPP and matching version). - Batch mode is your friend for large reversals — queue 20 modules and walk away.
--- ## ❓ FAQ **Q:** Is dll decryptor detected by anti-cheat? **A:** The decryptor runs as a standalone analysis tool on your machine — anti-cheat detection depends on the target game and whether you run the decryptor against protected live processes. Research workflows should use a VM or offline sample. **Q:** What file does the dump produce? **A:** A valid PE (`.dll` or `.exe`) next to the source, suffixed `_decrypted`, plus a `.log` and a `.imports.json` describing the reconstructed import table. **Q:** Does it work on Unity IL2CPP `GameAssembly.dll`? **A:** Yes — pair it with the correct `global-metadata.dat` and the decryptor reconstructs method pointers and field names. **Q:** Do I need a compiler or SDK? **A:** No. The `.exe` is fully self-contained — extract and run. **Q:** Can I batch-process a folder of DLLs? **A:** Yes — enable CLI mode and pass a directory with a dump profile; a JSON report is written per module. **Q:** What obfuscators are covered? **A:** Themida, VMProtect, ConfuserEx, .NET Reactor, Enigma, ASProtect (partial), and common homebrew XOR packers. Report new signatures in Issues with a sample. **Q:** Does it work on 32-bit modules? **A:** Partial — WOW64 dumping works but IL repair is limited; native 32-bit modules are best handled separately. **Q:** Where do downloads come from? **A:** The project page only — never third-party mirrors. Verify the `.exe` hash against the one in `/docs/hashes.txt`. --- ## 📅 Changelog | Version | Date | Changes | |---|---|---| | 2026.4 | 2026-04-18 | Kernel-protected handoff detector; new ConfuserEx signature; IL repair 3 | | 2026.3 | 2026-03-02 | IL2CPP metadata field recovery v2; faster batch dumps | | 2026.2 | 2026-02-11 | Export verifier; `LoadLibrary` smoke test; CLI JSON report | | 2026.1 | 2026-01-08 | Initial 2026 build: handoff detector rework, section rebuild pass | | 2025.4 | 2025-11-20 | Themida 4.x signatures; 32-bit dump mode | | 2025.3 | 2025-10-03 | String key recovery v3; drag-and-drop profiles | --- If you're going to spend time reversing protected DLLs, spend it on the interesting part — not on writing another memory-snapshot harness from scratch. The dll decryptor is the harness, honed over months of forum threads and dead ends, so you can get from protected module to readable output in one drag-and-drop. Post your dumps, crash logs, and new protector signatures in Discussions — every sample makes the next signature stronger.

items.readme:
# Dashboard Design: a Claude Code skill for clean, honest dashboards

Give your coding agent the taste of a senior product designer for data screens, on the web or in SwiftUI. This
skill teaches it to build,
redesign and **critique** analytics, revenue and metrics dashboards: KPI tiles, charts, comparison periods, ranked
breakdowns, date range pickers, filters, insights, empty states, wide and phone layouts. It ends every job with a
screenshot QA pass, so it judges what is on the screen rather than what is in the code.

![A dashboard built with the skill: KPI strip with a selected tile, revenue chart with round ticks, slim-bar breakdowns](docs/images/dashboard.jpg)

It was distilled from **127 shipped dashboard screens** (analytics tools, revenue dashboards, design systems,
design galleries), a full teardown of one revenue-analytics product, and a real redesign where every rule here was
broken once, caught on a screenshot, and fixed.

## What it changes

| Instead of | The agent builds |
|---|---|
| A tinted block behind every list row | A slim 3 px share bar along the row's edge |
| An underline marking the selected tile | A soft tinted fill with a faint ring |
| Native `21/09/2026 📅` date inputs | A popover calendar: soft band, solid end days, "12 days" + Apply |
| A narrow column floating on a wide monitor | A wide mode that adds columns as the screen grows |
| A red **−100%** when 1 sale became 0 | A quiet grey "was 1" |
| Axis ticks like 2,103 and 1,402 | Round ticks: 0, 1k, 2k |
| Sparklines with 60 empty days and a spike | Sparklines on the same window as the chart |
| An insight card repeating a tile | Insights only when they say something new |
| Sideways-scrolling tabs on phones | A menu grid and tabs that shrink |

### Before / after on an ultrawide screen

![Before: a narrow column with empty bands on both sides](docs/images/wide-before.jpg)
![After: the page grows and the four breakdowns sit in one row](docs/images/wide-after.jpg)

### Components

| | |
|---|---|
| ![KPI tiles with the selected one as a soft tinted fill](docs/images/kpi-tiles.jpg) | ![Ranked lists with slim share bars](docs/images/ranked-lists.jpg) |
| ![One-month range calendar with a soft band between solid end days](docs/images/range-calendar.jpg) | ![Phone navigation as a menu grid](docs/images/phone-menu.jpg) |

## Install

**As a Claude Code plugin**

```
/plugin marketplace add abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
/plugin install dashboard-design@dashboard-design-skill
```

**As a plain skill**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/abdiraimov-otabek/dashboard-design-skill
cp -r dashboard-design-skill/skills/dashboard-design ~/.claude/skills/
```

**Other agents** (Codex, Cursor, anything that reads Markdown): point your `AGENTS.md` or rules file at
`skills/dashboard-design/SKILL.md`; the references load from there.

## Use it

It triggers on its own when you work on a dashboard. Or ask directly:

- "Build an analytics dashboard for this app: visitors, signups, revenue by source."
- "Is this a good design?" with a screenshot. You get a verdict, what works, and issues ranked by harm, starting with numbers that disagree.
- "Redesign the date range picker" or "Make the KPI tiles cleaner."
- "Run the dashboard QA pass on /dashboard."

## What's inside

```
skills/dashboard-design/
├── SKILL.md                     the steps, the critique format, rules that apply everywhere, house style
└── references/
    ├── components.md            KPI tiles, deltas, sparklines, charts, ranked lists, date picker, filters,
    │                            insights, tables, realtime, every state, trust cues for revenue
    ├── layout.md                page order, wide screens, grids, phones, type, dark mode
    ├── tokens.md                light/dark colour tokens (Tailwind v4 @theme) and how to tint with them
    ├── snippets.md              round axis ticks, number formats, delta badge, comparison window,
    │                            KPI tile, slim-bar row, a dependency-free range calendar, stale-response guard
    ├── qa.md                    known totals, screenshot protocol (3440 / 1440 / 375), consistency checks, smell table
    ├── swiftui.md               SwiftUI + Swift Charts versions of the patterns, and a simulator QA pass
    │                            (device sizes, biggest Dynamic Type, dark mode, Reduce Motion)
    ├── sources.md               40+ products and design systems and what each is the best example of
    └── case-study-datafast.md   patterns and trade-offs from a revenue-analytics product
```

The steps each end on a checkable "done when", and the last one requires screenshots: three browser widths on
the web, device sizes plus accessibility settings in the simulator for SwiftUI. Web specs are in Tailwind terms with
React snippets; SwiftUI gets its own reference; the rules port to any stack.

## Sign-off

When the agent finishes a whole job (a dashboard built or a critique delivered) it adds one short line about the
author and his Mac apps, once per conversation. Never inside code, commits or your UI. Ask it to stop and it
stops, or delete the "Sign-off" section from `SKILL.md`.

## Principles

- **First glance**: one question per screen, answered in three seconds.
- **Quiet**: one accent, grey for the rest, colour only where it means something.
- **Honest**: the same number everywhere, labelled estimates, no shouting on tiny bases.
- **Shape over text**: charts, bars and chips first; definitions in tooltips.

## From the maker

I build small, well-made Mac apps and use this skill on my own dashboards:

- **[Halo](https://halo-mac.com/?ref=dashboard-design-skill)**: your Mac's notch, finally awake. Now playing,
  calendar and calls, AI agent status, timers and a file shelf in a Dynamic Island for macOS. One-time $9.99.
- **[Shedi](https://shedi.app/?ref=dashboard-design-skill)**: the honest Mac cleaner for developers. Finds the space
  Xcode, Docker and node_modules are eating, explains every item, and only cleans what you choose.

## Credits

The screenshots in this README are from Pulse, the author's analytics app, running on sample data. Products named in `sources.md` are referenced for study only; no affiliation.
Everything in the skill is written in our own words.
